# s271 — Add the process lessons from dogfooding to slicer ai relay and ai instructions

Several relay practices that kept runs correct and cheap in this repo live only in one orchestrator's private memory, where other agents, other vendors and the owner cannot see them: a temp directory per role, reviewers that make no git writes, the orchestrator reading the diff itself, landing parallel slices one at a time, running the full suite once, and compacting the session between slices. This slice moves the generic ones into `slicer ai relay` and the compaction rule into `slicer ai instructions`, so every slicer user's agents get them.

**Findings:** owner, 2026-10-14: relay practices live only in the orchestrator's private memory; owner chose ai relay for generic rules and asked that instructions say to compact where it makes most sense · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-15** — Verified outcome for s271. The slice relay and the instructions carry the seven dogfooding rules, all in src/slicer/ai.py, pinned by tests/test_ai.py:
(1) Every brief names the role's own temp directory, and no two agents share one. Lives in the Every brief section of RELAY_ORDER.
(2) Reviewer, architect and gate briefs forbid git writes; a needed write stops and goes to the owner. Every brief section.
(3) The orchestrator reads the implementer's diff before review, and reruns the tests only as Order says. Roles section (RELAY_HEAD).
(4) Suite: a whole-slice implementer runs the full suite once; in a split, parts run only their own tests and the orchestrator's run on the combined diff is the one full run; the orchestrator reruns the suite only if the diff changed after that run or main moved. Order section. The existing split sentence ("The orchestrator runs the full suite on the combined diff") is unchanged.
(5) Parallel slices run only with disjoint files, are reviewed and landed one at a time, and rerun the suite on the slice branch merged with the new main when main moved. Order section.
(6) Compaction in the relay: after a slice lands or hands off, and before briefing the next, compact the orchestrator session or start a fresh one; re-read state with slicer show ID --json --lean. Order section.
(7) INSTRUCTIONS: after the finish step and before claiming the next slice, compact or start a fresh session; state lives in slicer. It is in a new "## Between slices" section (BETWEEN_SLICES) after the hand-off section, in both the full text and --rest. It is not in "## Implement one slice" because that section was already 348 words against the test_Instructions_ImplementSection budget of under 350.
Also: docs/agents.md is unchanged (it quotes only the unchanged split sentence); CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Changed has one bullet.

## Why

The owner asked on 2026-10-14 where the relay process should be documented, chose the shipped `ai relay` text for generic rules, and asked that slicer's instructions tell agents to compact where it makes the most sense. Project policy stays in the role matrix, and repo commands stay in AGENTS.md. Today's relays ran the full suite three times per slice; the implementer's run alone would have done, plus a rerun when main moved. A long orchestrator session also carries every earlier slice's diffs and reports, which costs tokens and attention, while the state it needs lives in slicer.
